description: Table 2 is a single rendered table image (no plot, micrograph or schematic) titled "Calculated values for elastic constants (C_ij), bulk modulus (B), shear modulus (G), Young's modulus (E), hardness (H_V), B/G and Poisson's ratio (r) of Fe–Mn–Al alloys (GPa)". It has a header row (Species, C11, C12, C44, B, G, E, σ, H_V, B/G) and nine data rows giving computed properties for Fe1−xMnxAl in 12.5% Mn steps: FeAl (294.0, 133.7, 157.0, 187.1, 119.8, 296.2, 0.236, 16.5, 1.56); Fe0.875Mn0.125Al (265.2, 143.0, 150.4, 184.1, 105.0, 264.7, 0.260, 12.8, 1.75); Fe0.75Mn0.25Al (247.2, 148.8, 147.4, 181.9, 95.2, 243.2, 0.277, 10.5, 1.91); Fe0.625Mn0.375Al (236.2, 151.1, 141.0, 179.2, 88.2, 227.3, 0.288, 9.0, 2.03); Fe0.5Mn0.5Al (225.0, 152.0, 126.2, 176.3, 77.2, 202.1, 0.309, 6.7, 2.28); Fe0.375Mn0.625Al (230.1, 151.1, 134.7, 176.5, 86.1, 222.2, 0.290, 8.7, 2.05); Fe0.25Mn0.75Al (237.9, 141.0, 134.6, 173.3, 89.4, 228.8, 0.280, 9.8, 1.94); Fe0.125Mn0.875Al (255.2, 138.8, 154.2, 171.5, 85.6, 220.2, 0.286, 9.0, 2.00); MnAl (203.8, 152.9, 126.6, 169.8, 67.5, 178.8, 0.324, 5.0, 2.52). Within the Fe1−xMnxAl series the moduli E, G and hardness H_V all dip at Fe0.5Mn0.5Al while C12, σ and B/G peak there; B falls monotonically from FeAl to MnAl. The table supports the claim that all Fe1−xMnxAl alloys are mechanically stable, FeAl being the stiffest/hardest and MnAl the softest, with Poisson's ratios near 0.3 indicating metallic bonding.

subfigures.description: Single tabular panel: 10 columns (Species, C11, C12, C44, B, G, E, σ, H_V, B/G) and 9 composition rows from FeAl through Fe0.875Mn0.125Al to MnAl; all cells numerically legible; elastic constants and moduli in GPa, σ and B/G dimensionless.

observations.observation: The table lists nine Fe1−xMnxAl compositions from FeAl to MnAl in 12.5% Mn increments (FeAl, Fe0.875Mn0.125Al, Fe0.75Mn0.25Al, Fe0.625Mn0.375Al, Fe0.5Mn0.5Al, Fe0.375Mn0.625Al, Fe0.25Mn0.75Al, Fe0.125Mn0.875Al, MnAl).

FeAl has the highest C11 (294.0 GPa), highest C44 (157.0 GPa), highest B (187.1 GPa), highest G (119.8 GPa), highest E (296.2 GPa), highest H_V (16.5 GPa), lowest σ (0.236) and lowest B/G (1.56) of all rows.
MnAl has the lowest C11 (203.8 GPa), lowest B (169.8 GPa), lowest G (67.5 GPa), lowest E (178.8 GPa), lowest H_V (5.0 GPa), highest σ (0.324) and highest B/G (2.52).
The bulk modulus B decreases monotonically across the series: 187.1, 184.1, 181.9, 179.2, 176.3, 176.5, 173.3, 171.5, 169.8 GPa for FeAl → MnAl.

Within the Fe1−xMnxAl rows (excluding MnAl) the minima of C44 (126.2 GPa), E (202.1 GPa), G (77.2 GPa) and H_V (6.7 GPa) and the maximum of C12 (152.0 GPa), σ (0.309) and B/G (2.28) all occur at Fe0.5Mn0.5Al.

The citing text states that Fe0.5Mn0.5Al has the lowest C11 value of 225.0 GPa, but the table shows MnAl with a lower C11 of 203.8 GPa; the text's 'lowest' claim holds only within the Fe1−xMnxAl series excluding MnAl.
The citing text states that FeAl has the highest C11 value of 294.0 GPa, indicating FeAl is highly incompressible under uniaxial stress along the crystallographic x-axis (ε11).
The citing text states that MnAl and FeAl have the smallest and largest C44 values of 126.6 and 157.0 GPa respectively, and that C44 represents the shear modulus on the (100) crystal planes.
The citing text states the bulk modulus values of the Fe1−xMnxAl system are 187.1, 184.1, 181.9, 179.2, 176.3, 176.5, 173.3, 171.5 and 169.8 GPa for FeAl through MnAl, matching the table.
The citing text states the Poisson's ratio of the Fe1−xMnxAl system ranges from 0.236 to 0.324 and that values close to 0.3 indicate strong metallic bonding.

The citing text states that these Fe–Mn–Al alloys are mechanically stable structures because they satisfy the cubic-system mechanical stability criteria, and that B, G, E and Poisson's ratio were obtained by the Voigt–Reuss–Hill (VRH) approximation.
The caption labels the Poisson's ratio column as (r), whereas the table column header itself is printed as σ; the numeric entries are the same quantity.
The caption attributes all tabulated quantities (C_ij, B, G, E, H_V, B/G, Poisson's ratio) to Fe–Mn–Al alloys with units of GPa.

The citing text relates the table to Figs. 5–7, noting that Young's modulus and C11−C12 follow a similar variation trend, that shear modulus and C44 show a similar trend, and that Poisson's ratio and B/G vary similarly with Mn content.
